title: The Personal Organization Landscape
description: Personal organization — the individual’s operating system — spans: the capture (the getting it out of the head), the clarify (the deciding what it means), the organize (the parking it where it belongs), the plan (the choosing the work), the execute (the doing), and the review (the reflecting). The philosophies: the GTD (the mind like water — the stress-free), the time-blocking (the calendar as the plan), the bullet journal (the analog mindful), the second brain (the knowledge compounding), the essentialist (the less but better), and the anti-system (the structured procrastination — the Perry). The principle: the system serves the person — the chosen by fit, the adapted by experience, the sustained by review.
key_points: Capture, clarify, organize, plan, execute, review: the universal pipeline
GTD, time-blocking, bullet journal, second brain, essentialism
Fit over fashion in system choice
Adapted by experience; sustained by review
how_it_works: Survey philosophies, choose by fit, install pipeline, adapt, review regularly.

title: Capture Systems Compared
description: Capture — the getting it out of the head — systems: the ubiquitous (the always-with — the phone, the notebook; the Allen’s rule), the inbox (the single — the processed; the multiple — the consolidated), the voice (the recorded — the transcribed), the quick-add (the frictionless — the two-tap), and the sweep (the mind — the weekly; the complete). The disciplines: the immediacy (the captured — the within seconds), the completeness (the everything — the trusted), and the processing (the emptied — the regularly). The tools: the analog (the pocket notebook — the reliable), and the digital (the apps — the synced). The principle: the captured mind is the clear mind — the ubiquitous, the immediate, the processed.
key_points: Ubiquitous capture tools always at hand
how_it_works: Carry capture always, inbox everything, sweep mind weekly, process to zero.

title: Planning Systems Compared
description: Planning — the choosing — systems: the daily (the MITs — the 3 most important; the Ivy Lee — the 6), the weekly (the reviewed — the planned; the Franklin’s), the quarterly (the goals — the 12-week year), the yearly (the themes — the resolutions; the backward-designed), and the anti-planning (the emergent — the responsive). The horizons: the day (the executed), the week (the managed), the quarter (the achieved), the year (the directed), and the life (the envisioned). The disciplines: the written (the planned — the on paper), the realistic (the capacity — the honored), and the reviewed (the compared — the actual). The principle: the planned life is the intended — the horizon-nested, the written, the realistic.
key_points: Daily MITs; weekly reviews; quarterly goals; yearly themes
how_it_works: Plan yearly themes, quarterly goals, weekly reviews, daily MITs; nest horizons.

title: Prioritization Frameworks
description: Prioritization — the choosing what matters — frameworks: the Eisenhower (the urgent/important — the 4 quadrants), the ABCDE (the Tracy — the lettered; the eaten frog), the MoSCoW (the must/should/could/won’t), the Pareto (the 80/20 — the vital few), the ICE/RICE (the scored — the product), the cost of delay (the weighted — the WSJF), and the single (the one thing — the Keller; the essentialist — the McKeown). The use: the daily (the MITs — the chosen), the project (the sequenced), and the life (the vision-aligned). The disciplines: the important (the protected — the scheduled), the said-no (the declined — the gracefully), and the reviewed (the reprioritized — the regularly). The principle: the prioritized life is the meaningful — the important scheduled, the trivial declined.
key_points: Eisenhower, ABCDE, MoSCoW, Pareto, RICE, One Thing
Schedule the important; decline the trivial
how_it_works: Frame choices, apply fitting framework, schedule important, decline rest, reprioritize.

title: Routine Systems
description: Routines — the automated days — systems: the morning (the launched — the Miracle Morning’s SAVERS; the personalized), the evening (the shut down — the Newport’s; the reviewed), the workday (the structured — the deep blocks; the breaks), and the weekly (the anchored — the review, the planning, the rest). The design: the anchored (the habit-stacked — the existing), the minimal (the started — the tiny; the expanded), the tracked (the checked — the streaked), and the flexible (the traveled — the adapted). The virtues: the decision-free (the automated), the momentum (the started — the rolling), and the identity (the lived — the “I am”). The vices: the rigid (the broken — the abandoned), and the performative (the posted — the not the lived). The principle: the routined day runs itself — the designed minimally, the stacked on anchors, the flexed when needed.
key_points: Morning launch; evening shutdown; structured workday
how_it_works: Design minimal routines, stack on anchors, track, flex when disrupted.

title: Review Systems
description: Reviews — the reflecting — systems: the daily (the 5-minute — the done, the learned, the tomorrow), the weekly (the GTD — the comprehensive; the 60–90 minutes), the monthly (the goals — the checked; the themes), the quarterly (the 12-week — the scored; the reset), the yearly (the past year — the reviewed; the new — the designed), and the project (the post-mortemed — the learned). The disciplines: the scheduled (the calendared — the kept), the honest (the faced — the numbers), and the actioned (the lessons — the applied). The principle: the reviewed life improves — the reflected regularly, the honest always, the applied consistently.
key_points: Daily 5-min; weekly GTD; monthly; quarterly; yearly
how_it_works: Calendar reviews at each horizon, reflect honestly, extract lessons, apply.

title: Tool Systems: Analog vs Digital
description: Tool choice — the analog vs digital — weighs: the analog (the paper — the focused; the memorable — the handwritten; the limited — the unsearchable), the digital (the synced — the searchable; the distracting — the notified), the hybrid (the bullet journal plus the calendar — the best of both), and the minimal (the one app — the mastered). The selection: the friction (the lowest — the winning), the trust (the relied — the backed-up), and the joy (the used — the liked). The principle: the tool serves — the frictionless, the trusted, the liked; the system matters more than the app.
how_it_works: Assess friction, choose by fit, master one tool, hybridize deliberately.

title: The Anti-Productivity Critique
description: The critique — the productivity questioned — argues: the neoliberal (the self-optimizing — the demanded; the resisted), the burnout (the optimized — the exhausted), the meaning (the efficient — the empty), and the alternatives (the rest — the honored; the enough — the embraced; the slow — the valued). The integrations: the sustainable (the paced), the values-aligned (the meaningful), and the humane (the rested). The principle: the productivity serves the life — the questioned regularly, the balanced wisely, the human kept.
how_it_works: Question regularly, align with values, honor rest, embrace enough.

title: The 12 Week Year
description: The 12 Week Year (Moran and Lennington) — the annualized quarter — runs: the vision (the compelling — the 3-year; the emotional), the goals (the 2–3 — the 12-week; the specific), the plan (the weekly — the tactics; the daily — the executed), the scorecard (the weekly — the execution-scored; the 85% — the targeted), and the accountability (the WAM — the weekly accountability meeting; the peer). The disciplines: the execution (the great — the focus of the book), the measurement (the lead and lag), and the time (the intentional — the blocked). The principle: the year in 12 weeks — the urgency healthy, the execution great, the accountability peered.
how_it_works: Vision 3 years, goal 12 weeks, plan weekly, execute daily, score weekly, meet accountably.

title: Essentialism: Less but Better
description: Essentialism (McKeown) — the disciplined pursuit of less — practices: the explore (the options — the many; the discerned), the eliminate (the trivial — the many; the said-no — the gracefully), and the execute (the essential — the few; the protected — the routined). The mindsets: the choice (the “I choose to”), the discernment (the “if it isn’t a clear yes, it’s a no”), and the trade-off (the embraced — the real). The disciplines: the sleep (the protected), the play (the honored), and the boundaries (the drawn — the socially). The principle: the essential pursued — the explored widely, the eliminated ruthlessly, the executed effortlessly.
how_it_works: Explore options, discern essential, eliminate trivial, execute with routine.

title: The PARA Method (Overview)
description: PARA (Forte) — the universal organizer — sorts: the Projects (the active — the goaled; the short-term), the Areas (the maintained — the standarded; the ongoing), the Resources (the referenced — the interested; the future-use), and the Archives (the inactive — the completed; the retrievable). The principle: the organized by actionability — the projects first, the archives last; the every-note has a home. (Full depth in the Second Brain database.)
how_it_works: Sort by actionability, file accordingly, archive completed, retrieve when needed.

title: Getting Results the Agile Way
description: Agile Results (Meier) — the personal Scrum — runs: the 3 wins (the daily — the chosen; the achieved), the Monday vision (the weekly — the 3 outcomes), the Friday reflection (the weekly — the 3 lessons), the monthly (the 3 improvements), and the yearly (the 3 aspirations). The principles: the boundaries (the hot spots — the mind, body, emotions, career, finance, relationships, fun; the balanced), the freshness (the 3 — the daily renewal), and the strength (the weaknesses — the spent less on). The principle: the results agile — the 3 wins daily, the reflected weekly, the balanced across hot spots.
key_points: Hot spots balanced: mind to fun
how_it_works: Choose 3 wins, vision Monday, reflect Friday, improve monthly, balance hotspots.

title: The Eisenhower Matrix in Depth
description: The Eisenhower Matrix — the urgent/important — quadrants: the Q1 (the urgent-important — the crises; the managed, the minimized), the Q2 (the non-urgent-important — the quality; the scheduled, the maximized — the Covey’s focus), the Q3 (the urgent-unimportant — the interruptions; the delegated, the declined), and the Q4 (the neither — the time-wasters; the eliminated). The practice: the weekly (the sorted — the tasks; the scheduled Q2), the audit (the time — the tracked; the quadrants — the revealed), and the shift (the Q1-to-Q2 — the migrated by planning). The principle: the Q2 lived — the important scheduled before the urgent, the crises prevented by the quality.
key_points: Q1 crises; Q2 quality; Q3 interruptions; Q4 waste
Maximize Q2; minimize Q1 via planning
how_it_works: Sort tasks weekly, schedule Q2 first, delegate Q3, eliminate Q4, audit time.

title: The Ivy Lee Method
description: The Ivy Lee (1918; the Schwab $25,000) — the six tasks — runs: the evening (the 6 — the tomorrow’s most important; the written), the ordered (the prioritized — the true order), the morning (the first — the single-tasked; the completed before the next), the unfinished (the moved — the tomorrow’s), and the repeated (the daily — the compounded). The virtues: the simplicity (the 6), the focus (the single), and the closure (the completed). The limits: the inflexible (the emergent — the unaccommodated), and the shallow (the deep — the unplanned). The principle: the six done — the prioritized nightly, the single-tasked daily, the compounded.
how_it_works: Write 6 nightly, order truly, work singly to completion, carry forward, repeat.

title: The Kanban Personal System
description: Personal kanban (Benson) — the visual workflow — boards: the options (the backlog — the all), the doing (the WIP-limited — the 3; the focused), and the done (the completed — the celebrated). The rules: the visualize (the all work — the seen), the limit (the WIP — the honored), and the flow (the pulled — the completed). The virtues: the visibility (the status — the at-a-glance), the limits (the overload — the prevented), and the flow (the smooth). The principle: the visualized work flows — the limited WIP, the pulled completion.
how_it_works: Board the work, limit doing, pull to done, visualize, celebrate completion.

title: The Autofocus System
description: Autofocus (Forster) — the intuition-trusting — runs: the list (the everything — the long; the unprioritized), the scan (the read-through — the ready-feeling), the work (the ready — the until the readiness fades), the dismiss (the resisted-long — the dropped), and the re-list (the remaining — the rewritten). The philosophy: the subconscious (the trusted — the creative; the knowing), and the standing-out (the noticed — the done). The virtues: the natural (the energy-honoring), and the creative (the friendly). The vices: the important-unready (the avoided), and the structureless (the drifting). The principle: the ready work works — the trusted intuition, the dismissed resistance.
how_it_works: List everything, scan for readiness, work until fade, dismiss resisted, re-list.

title: The 1-3-5 Rule
description: The 1-3-5 (the 1 big, 3 medium, 5 small) — the daily capacity — plans: the 1 (the big — the MIT; the deep), the 3 (the medium — the significant), the 5 (the small — the quick), and the total (the 9 — the realistic day). The virtues: the realistic (the capacity-honoring), and the balanced (the big-to-small). The principle: the 9 planned — the 1 that matters most, the honored capacity.
how_it_works: Choose 1-3-5 nightly, protect the big, complete in order of energy.

title: The Now Habit and Unscheduling
description: Unscheduling (Fiore’s Now Habit) — the guilt-free play — reverses: the schedule (the fixed — the play, the rest, the appointments — the first), the work (the fitted — the around the life; the 30-minute starts), and the guilt (the dropped — the play earned). The psychology: the procrastination (the perfectionism — the addressed; the “I have to” — the “I choose to”), and the starting (the 30-minute — the doable). The principle: the play scheduled first — the guilt dropped, the work chosen, the started small.
how_it_works: Calendar play/rest/appointments, fit work between, start with 30 minutes, drop guilt.

title: The Weekly Review (Universal)
description: The universal weekly review — the GTD-derived, system-agnostic — covers: the clear (the inboxes — the emptied; the mind — the swept), the current (the calendar — the past and future; the waiting-fors — the checked), the projects (the list — the reviewed; the next actions — the defined), the plan (the week — the previewed; the MITs — the chosen), and the reflect (the wins — the celebrated; the lessons — the noted). The logistics: the 60–90 minutes (the calendared — the sacred), the checklist (the followed), and the ritual (the enjoyed — the coffee). The principle: the week reviewed — the cleared, the current, the planned, the celebrated.
key_points: Preview week; choose MITs; celebrate wins
how_it_works: Calendar 60–90 min, follow checklist, clear, review, plan, reflect.

title: Choosing Your System: The Decision Guide
t: Choosing Your System: The Decision Guide
description: System choice — the decision — weighs: the work (the knowledge — the GTD/PARA; the creative — the bullet journal; the managerial — the time-blocking), the temperament (the analytical — the systematic; the intuitive — the flexible), the tools (the digital — the apps; the analog — the paper), the season (the overloaded — the capture-first; the drifting — the planning-first), and the experiment (the 30-day — the trialed; the kept — the what works). The combining: the hybrid (the GTD capture — the time-blocked execution — the journal reflection; the best-of). The principle: the system chosen and combined — the fitted, the trialed 30 days, the hybridized wisely.
key_points: Match system to work type and temperament
Consider tool preference and life season
how_it_works: Assess work and temperament, trial 30 days, keep what works, combine best parts.

title: The Hybrid Personal OS
description: The hybrid — the best-of-breed — combines: the capture (the GTD — the ubiquitous), the knowledge (the PARA — the second brain), the planning (the time-blocking — the calendar), the reflection (the bullet journal — the mindful), the habits (the atomic — the stacked), and the review (the weekly — the GTD). The design: the pipeline (the connected — the capture to review), the tools (the few — the integrated), and the simplicity (the maintained — the pruned). The principle: the hybrid serves — the best parts combined, the pipeline connected, the simplicity kept.
key_points: GTD capture + PARA knowledge + time-blocked execution
how_it_works: Adopt best parts, connect pipeline, integrate few tools, prune quarterly.

title: The Minimalist Personal OS
description: The minimalist — the least that works — keeps: the list (the one — the MITs), the calendar (the appointments — the only), the notebook (the capture — the single), and the review (the weekly — the 20-minute). The virtues: the sustainable (the kept — the forever), the clear (the uncluttered), and the free (the tool-independent). The principle: the least that organizes — the one list, the one calendar, the one notebook, the weekly glance.
key_points: One MIT list; one calendar; one notebook
how_it_works: Keep one list, one calendar, one notebook; review 20 min weekly.

title: Personal OS for Parents
description: The parent’s OS — the interrupted — adapts: the capture (the instant — the chaotic), the planning (the flexible — the 1-MIT days), the time (the stolen — the early mornings; the protected), the systems (the family — the shared calendar; the delegated), and the grace (the imperfect — the accepted). The principle: the parent organized — the flexible, the 1-MIT, the graced.
key_points: Shared family calendar; grace for imperfection
how_it_works: Capture instantly, plan 1 MIT, steal time early, share family calendar, accept imperfection.

title: The Personal OS Audit
description: The audit — the system’s health — assesses: the capture (the trusted — the complete), the planning (the realistic — the honored), the execution (the focused — the completed), the review (the kept — the learned), and the joy (the felt — the sustained). The cadence: the quarterly — the honest. The principle: the audited system serves — the assessed honestly, the pruned ruthlessly, the kept joyfully.
key_points: Assess capture, planning, execution, review, joy
how_it_works: Assess five dimensions quarterly, prune what fails, keep what serves.
